newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin vetoes law capping foreign share in UES.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin vetoes law capping foreign share in UES.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has vetoed a law setting the state share in national power company Unified Energy System (UES) at 51 percent and limiting non-resident ownership at 25 percent, the president's press service said on Wednesday.

The law was passed by the State Duma lower house of parliament on June 20 and by the Federation Council upper house on July 3. Foreign shareholders own 27.8 percent of RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES), Russia's biggest company by market capitalisation, according to the company's annual report.

The Russian state currently holds 52.7 percent of UES. The law had also stipulated that the state should transfer 33 percent to Russian regions, to be held individually by them in proportion to their electricity consumption.

Yeltsin is meeting First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is responsible for restructuring the energy sector, on Wednesday and they were due to discuss a presidential decree authorising UES to issue convertible bonds.
